subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Bank Runs and Self-Fulfilling Panic
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bank Runs and Self-Fulfilling Panic usable.

hook.text: Northern Rock was solvent until queues formed outside branches in 2007. The panic itself caused the insolvency.

buildup.text: A bank run is a self-fulfilling prophecy. If everyone believes the bank will fail and withdraws, the bank fails.

discovery.text: Diamond and Dybvig modeled this: even a healthy bank can't survive if all depositors withdraw at once.

twist.text: Deposit insurance was invented to break the cycle. If deposits are guaranteed, there's no reason to panic.

climax.text: Self-fulfilling prophecies appear in markets, rumors, and politics. When belief causes the outcome, perception.

punchline.text: The fear of a crash can cause the crash itself.

quiz.question: What makes a bank run self-fulfilling?
options: The bank secretly hides losses from customers
Mass withdrawal caused by fear of insolvency makes the bank actually insolvent
Government regulators force the bank to close

details.summary: Bank runs occur when depositors rush to withdraw money because they believe others will do the same. The fear becomes self-fulfilling: a solvent bank can become insolvent simply because enough people expect it to fail and act on that expectation.
details.whyItMatters: Bank runs demonstrate how social beliefs create economic reality. They show that financial stability depends not just on fundamentals but on collective confidence, making trust a genuine economic asset.
takeaways: Panic withdrawals can destroy a healthy bank through self-fulfilling prophecy
Each person's rational response to fear creates the feared outcome collectively
Deposit insurance was designed specifically to break the cycle of bank run panics

faq.question: How can a healthy bank fail from a bank run?
faq.answer: Banks keep only a fraction of deposits as cash, lending the rest. If enough depositors demand withdrawals simultaneously, even a solvent bank runs out of cash. Forced asset liquidation at fire-sale prices then creates actual insolvency from perceived insolvency.

faq.question: How does deposit insurance prevent bank runs?
faq.answer: When deposits are insured by the government, depositors have no reason to panic even if they fear the bank might fail. Removing the incentive to withdraw preemptively breaks the self-fulfilling cycle that turns fear into reality.
